11 Claude skills for day trading on NSE and BSE. Scan EQ charts, track NSE announcements, time every entry and exit in IST, replay the outcome with honest fills, then print a paper ticket. No broker login. No API key. No paid feed.

A scan is a list of charts that match a rule, not a list of stocks to buy. Most people who day trade lose money.

The eleven:
• /bazaar-scanner — NSE EQ bhavcopy universe, daily setups, 09:15 IST opening-range breakout
• /bazaar-news — NSE corporate announcements, tagged in IST
• /bazaar-entry — first completed bar beyond the range; forming bars wait
• /bazaar-exit — stop and target in rupees, flat by 15:15 IST
• /bazaar-timemachine — 10,000 IST-session replays
• /bazaar-risk — one slot, skip 11:15–13:15, paper only, PASS or BLOCK
• /bazaar-budget — size in INR, charges in the max-loss picture
• /bazaar-broker — generic paper ticket; typed yes only; never sends the order
• /bazaar-alerts — stop, target, 15:15 flatten, opening bell at 09:15 IST
• /bazaar-analyst — quarterly numbers; never a buy call
• /bazaar-smartmoney — NSE bulk/block deals and FII-DII cash (there is no Indian Pelosi feed)

Pipeline: scanner → news → entry → exit → time machine → budget → risk → broker.

Honest fills: first print strictly after the signal, 0.15% equity slip (0.5pt on index options), stop at the traded extreme not the theoretical stop, NSE statutory charges plus a typical Rs 20/order. A 10:30 day-type label is not used on a 09:15 or 10:00 bar. Empty FII/OI stays empty. --demo is not live.

Works fully offline on tests/fixtures/. The tools do not call the network. Live NSE pages are unofficial and rate-limited — drop your own files in the same shapes.

Not financial advice. A yes covers one ticket. “yes to all” is refused. A stop is a plan, not a guarantee.

🚨 NSE’s New Retail Algo Trading Rules: Is Algo Trading Becoming Difficult for Ordinary Retail Traders?

NSE Circular No. 58/2026 | November 20, 2026

10 Critical Questions:

1. Static IP access is intended only for tech-savvy retail investors who develop their own algos using programming knowledge.

2. Retail traders who depend on third-party algo providers may face restrictions on Static IP access.

3. Does understanding markets, options strategies and risk management no longer suffice? Must every algo trader also become a programmer?

4. What happens to traders using no-code and low-code algo platforms?

5. Will retail traders now need to hire programmers and build their own technology infrastructure?

6. If an algo strategy is developed with professional assistance, how will the trader qualify under the new definition?

7. Will smaller algo providers find it increasingly difficult to serve retail clients?

8. Will compliance costs and regulatory uncertainty discourage retail participation in algo trading?

9. Large institutions have technology teams and infrastructure. How will independent retail traders compete?

10. Most importantly, what is the practical alternative for an ordinary retail trader who understands trading but does not know programming?

MY CONCERN:

Investor protection is absolutely necessary. However, regulation must strike a balance between risk management and accessibility.

Algo trading should become safer, more transparent and more accessible — not a privilege limited to people with programming skills.

SEBI and NSE must clarify how ordinary retail traders can practically access compliant third-party algo solutions under this framework.

A simple question:

ARE WE PROTECTING RETAIL TRADERS OR CREATING NEW BARRIERS TO RETAIL ALGO TRADING?

AlgoTrader is a Claude Code skill for builders working on quantitative trading systems for Indian equity markets with Zerodha/Kite workflows.

It helps you move from idea to a safer implementation by combining a bot-generation wizard, NSE universe fetching, backtest/live checks, and a documented set of trading-system gotchas.

Key features:

• Interactive bot wizard – scans existing code and asks about trade style, universe, capital, and risk tolerance
• Zerodha/Kite workflow guidance – covers tick-size rounding, position reconciliation, stop-loss lifecycle, and credentials setup
• Live universe fetcher – creates JSON files for Nifty 50, Nifty 100, Midcap 150, and Smallcap 250 constituents
• Backtest-live parity checks – documents data caching, VWAP reset, candle completion, and slippage issues that break live results
• Risk and analytics patterns – includes Kelly sizing, portfolio heat, regime detection, structured logs, and post-trade reporting

It’s open-source (MIT license).

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
BREAKING: I turned Claude into a fundamental analyst for NSE stocks.

Type one stock name. It reads the results, the investor presentation and the concall, then grades the stock in 11 checks.

Here\'s what it checks ↓

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.author: HaseebBadar_Stocks
haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
Why I built it:

The chart tells you where the money is going.

The results tell you why, and whether the story is strong enough to hold through the pullbacks.

Chart first. Results second. It does the second part.

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.author: HaseebBadar_Stocks
haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
CHECK 1: COMMODITY OR SPECIALITY?

A commodity business stays cheap, even at a low PE.

A speciality business can stay expensive for years.

It classifies the business before looking at a single number.

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.author: HaseebBadar_Stocks
haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
CHECK 2: IS THE GROUP MOVING?

One stock rising alone in a dead sector gets rejected.

It looks for 4 or 5 peers moving together, because real themes move in packs.

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.author: HaseebBadar_Stocks
haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
CHECK 3: WHAT\'S THE TRIGGER?

New plant, order book, acquisition, a rule change that grows the market.

It pulls management\'s own claim from the presentation and puts a number on it.

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.author: HaseebBadar_Stocks
haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
CHECK 4: SPEEDING UP OR SLOWING DOWN?

Growth falling from 80% to 50% still looks great on paper.

The market punishes the slowdown anyway. It flags it.

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.author: HaseebBadar_Stocks
haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
CHECK 5 AND 6: WHO PAID FOR THE GROWTH, AND DID THE PROFIT TURN INTO CASH?

Growth paid for with debt is a warning.

Profit that never shows up as cash is a bigger one.

These are the checks almost everyone skips.

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.author: HaseebBadar_Stocks
haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
CHECK 7 AND 8: VALUATION, DONE PROPERLY

No "PE is high, avoid".

It works out the PEG, then a forward PE from management\'s own guidance, and shows the maths.

Then it sizes the capex against today\'s revenue.

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.author: HaseebBadar_Stocks
haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
CHECK 9 TO 11: MARKET SHARE, STAGE OF THE MOVE, AND THE GROWTH-FEAR CHECK

Is it early in the move, or already up 400%?

Is the company getting too big to keep growing?

haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.author: HaseebBadar_Stocks
haseeb-claude-fundamental-analyst.text:
THEN ONE VERDICT:

Leader-grade.
Trade only.
Watch and read.
Reject.

And one rule it never breaks: every number comes with a source and a date. If it can\'t find a number, it writes "not found". It never guesses.
